AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818)
937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is
discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance,
please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Devine announced that the Hollywood Burbank Airport will have a
  subcontractor community information session on September 12, at the Courtyard by Marriott
  in Burbank, to discuss replacing the passenger terminal. Devine advised council to wait on
  redistricting until the Santa Monica case was resolved and pause community outreach
  efforts.

  To increase attendance for the upcoming “Council in your Neighborhood” meeting,
  Councilmember Asatryan asked staff to send out flyers within the neighborhood in which the
  meeting will take place. Asatryan and Mayor Brotman attended the grand reopening of the
  Montrose Bowl. Asatryan met with city staff and the LA County Economic Development and
  Procurement Office to discuss moving forward on the local-owned, minority-owned and
  woman-owned businesses as part of the workplan. In celebration of Women’s Equality Day,
  Asatryan invited the public to attend a webinar about woman-owned or minority-owned
  business certification and how this might help businesses acquire government and private
  sector contracts. More information regarding the webinar can be found at
  www.chooseglendaleca.gov.

  Councilmember Kassakhian wanted to get more information to understand the Santa
  Monica districting case. He watched the film “Mildred Pierce,” which was shown by the
  Glendale Historical Society, in Brand Park.

  4
   Mayor Brotman and Councilmember Kassakhian spoke at a rally about the humanitarian
  crisis in Artsakh in front of the Azeri Consulate in Los Angeles. Brotman attended the Edible
  Food Recovery Working Group meeting, where SB-1383 – Organics Recycling was
  discussed. Brotman asked staff to provide a report on how the city is reaching out to the
  public about openings on boards and commissions and soliciting applications. Devine
  announced there is an opening on the Historic Preservation Commission.

  City Attorney Mike Garcia provided a brief explanation on the Santa Monica districting case.

  City Clerk Dr. Suzie Abajian explained that that the City Clerk’s office has been posting
  about the openings on Boards and Commissions and the application process on social
  media, in multiple languages. She also stated that the City webpage on boards and
  commissions has up-to-date information on all the open seats and the application process.
